newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QB BERNIE KOSAR ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QB BERNIE KOSAR ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.

text.p: Bernie Kosar, who spent most of his career as starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns but was relegated to third-string with the Miami Dolphins last season, announced his retirement on Monday.

Kosar passed for 23,301 yards and 124 touchdowns in a 12-year NFL career. He led Cleveland to the AFC Championship Game three times, but the Browns were beaten each time by John Elway and the Denver Broncos.

Kosar finally earned a Super Bowl ring with the Dallas Cowboys as a backup to Troy Aikman in 1993, playing a significant role in the NFC Championship Game that season when Aikman was knocked out with a concussion.
The 33-year-old Kosar led the University of Miami to a national championship in 1983 under coach Jimmy Johnson and played for the Browns from 1985 to 1993.

He was reunited with Johnson in Dallas and again in Miami in the latter stages of his career. Kosar spent his final three seasons with the Dolphins, last year as third string quarterback behind Dan Marino and Craig Erickson.
Kosar, an unrestricted free agent, had been expected to re-sign with Miami but instead informed Johnson of his intention to retire.
